Prevention: Plough 1-2 times; dry soil for 10-15 days before planting.
N leads to too much crop growth which favours the disease by increasing leaf wetness and humidity.
Increase plant spacing (25x25 cm) (depending on variety and soil) to increase aeration and reduce humidity.
Remove and burn crop residue to prevent rice blast from reoccurring.
If available, use certified disease-free seed.
Flood the field as often as possible.
Sow seeds early, when possible, after the onset of the rainy season.
Monitoring: Scout 3 times per week, scout every day when weather is wet and hot.
If you see symptoms of the disease on 5% of plants use
At early stage look for tiny red spot on the leaf or stem.
A typical blast lesion on a rice leaf is grey at the centre, has a dark border, and is diamond- shaped or spindle- shaped.
Direct Control: Remove infected/ diseased plants from field and destroy.
Restrictions: Spray at early tillering and pinnacle initiation to heading stage
Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
U (Unlikely to present acute health hazard)
